core_obligations: Set up flat and injective representatives: choose a K-flat complex T^bullet of flat A-modules representing R\Gamma(X, K), where A = \Gamma(X, O_X); let T^bullet \otimes_A O_X be the pullback along (X, O_X) -> (pt, A) with its adjunction map to K; use Lemma lemma-factor-through-K-flat to represent that map by a map into a K-flat complex K^bullet with flat terms; choose a K-injective complex I^bullet of injective O_X-modules representing M, and finally a quasi-isomorphism Tot(K^bullet \otimes I^bullet) -> J^bullet into a K-injective complex with injective terms (proof lines 8358-8389).

Write the comparison maps on every open: for any open W in X produce the composite Tot(T^bullet \otimes_A I^bullet(W)) -> Tot(K^bullet(W) \otimes_A I^bullet(W)) -> J^bullet(W) of A-modules representing R\Gamma(X, K) \otimes_A^L R\Gamma(W, M) -> R\Gamma(W, K \otimes^L M), and note that these maps are compatible with restriction (proof lines 8390-8404).

Assemble the commutative(!) diagram of complexes of A-modules whose columns are the Mayer-Vietoris short exact sequences for X = U \cup V applied to I^bullet and to J^bullet, using that Tot(T^bullet \otimes_A -) carries short exact sequences of complexes to short exact sequences because the terms of T^bullet are flat A-modules (proof lines 8405-8424).

Identify the two sides with the two Mayer-Vietoris triangles: the right column is the distinguished triangle of Lemma lemma-unbounded-mayer-vietoris for K \otimes^L M, while the left column is the exact functor R\Gamma(X, K) \otimes_A^L - applied to the triangle for M, so the displayed map of distinguished triangles follows from functoriality of taking the associated distinguished triangle (proof lines 8424-8430).
proof_roadmap: Choose T^bullet, K^bullet, I^bullet and J^bullet so that every derived tensor product involved is represented by an honest complex with flat or injective terms (proof lines 8358-8389).
Define the comparison maps R\Gamma(X, K) \otimes_A^L R\Gamma(W, M) -> R\Gamma(W, K \otimes^L M) for every open W, compatibly with restriction (proof lines 8390-8404).
Form the commutative diagram of complexes whose columns are the Mayer-Vietoris short exact sequences for I^bullet and J^bullet (proof lines 8405-8424).
Conclude with functoriality of the distinguished triangle associated to a short exact sequence of complexes (proof lines 8424-8430).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for X = U \cup V and objects K, M of D(O_X) the cup-product maps assemble into a map of distinguished triangles: the triangle of Lemma lemma-unbounded-mayer-vietoris for K \otimes^L M on the right, and the exact functor R\Gamma(X, K) \otimes_A^L - applied to the triangle for M on the left (statement lines 8328-8354). The proof cannot work with the abstract triangles alone. It first chooses a K-flat complex T^bullet of flat A-modules for R\Gamma(X, K), replaces the adjunction map T^bullet \otimes_A O_X -> K by a map into a K-flat complex K^bullet with flat terms (proof lines 8358-8379), chooses K-injective representatives I^bullet for M and J^bullet for K \otimes^L M, and only then writes the comparison maps Tot(T^bullet \otimes_A I^bullet(W)) -> J^bullet(W) for every open W (proof lines 8390-8404). The decisive step is the commutative diagram of complexes of A-modules whose columns are the Mayer-Vietoris short exact sequences, where flatness of the terms of T^bullet is exactly what makes Tot(T^bullet \otimes_A -) preserve short exactness (proof lines 8405-8424). What has to be supplied by hand is the choice of the four representatives and that diagram; the cited Mayer-Vietoris, K-flat and delta-functor results are standard prerequisites. The claim is H2.
